Earthquake Hazards Program
The USGS monitors and reports on earthquakes, assesses earthquake impacts and hazards, and conducts targeted research on the causes and effects of earthquakes. We undertake these activities as part of the larger National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program (NEHRP), a four-agency partnership established by Congress.

Reproducible event-bed correlation with uncertainty: pyCoreRelator
Reproducible event-bed correlation with uncertainty: pyCoreRelator
Stratigraphic correlation is fundamental to Earth science, yet conventional approaches rely heavily on subjective visual data matching. Automated algorithms such as dynamic time warping (DTW) provide reproducibility, but when sequences are subdivided into clearly defined stratigraphic units, DTW alone struggles to explore a vast range of correlation possibilities among these units and...
Authors
Larry Syu-Heng Lai, Zoltan Sylvester, Jacob A. Covault, Joan S. Gomberg, Nora M. Nieminski
By
Natural Hazards Mission Area
,
Earthquake Hazards Program
,
Earthquake Science Center
November 13, 2026
Outer-rise earthquakes in the Alaska-Aleutian subduction zone: Implications for mantle hydration and tsunami hazards
Outer-rise earthquakes in the Alaska-Aleutian subduction zone: Implications for mantle hydration and tsunami hazards
Outer-rise, plate-bending faults provide major pathways for water to penetrate deep into the incoming plate, reaching mantle depths, and pose potential tsunami hazards. The Alaska-Aleutian subduction zone is an excellent site for studying the relationship between plate-bending faulting, incoming plate hydration, and tsunami hazards because its structure and seismicity vary significantly...
Authors
Patrick R. Matulka, Douglas A. Wiens, Zongshan Li, Grace Barcheck, Geoffrey A. Abers, Natalia A. Ruppert
By
Natural Hazards Mission Area
,
Earthquake Hazards Program
,
Earthquake Science Center
October 28, 2026
A new amphibious earthquake catalog for the Alaska Peninsula: Training, testing, and applying machine learning earthquake picking in offshore and amphibious environments
A new amphibious earthquake catalog for the Alaska Peninsula: Training, testing, and applying machine learning earthquake picking in offshore and amphibious environments
The dual seismological developments of large-scale offshore observational networks and high-quality machine-learning earthquake detection and picking allow unprecedented seismicity detection in high hazard subduction zones. We develop a high resolution machine learning enhanced seismicity catalog for the Alaska Peninsula stretch of the Alaska-Aleutian Subduction Zone, which was...
Authors
Grace Barcheck, Natalia A. Ruppert

2027 Long-term National Seismic Hazard Models for the U.S. Territories of Guam, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, and American Samoa
The U.S. Geological Survey will publish an updated National Seismic Hazard Model for the Pacific territories of Guam, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, and American Samoa in 2027. These models were last updated in 2012.
